<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Basic Functionality</h2><a id="user-content-basic-functionality" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Basic Functionality" href="#basic-functionality"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">This macro tries to simplify the process of <strong>including</strong> a julia file inside a Pluto notebook with the possibility of <strong>reloading</strong> the file once its contents are updated.
The target file can be any valid julia file (including another Pluto notebook), and this macro simply performs the following steps:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Create an empty temporary module (outside of the Pluto workspace)</li>
<li>Include the target file within the temporary module</li>
<li>Explicitly imports (from the module created in 1.) the <em>names</em> defined in the <strong>included</strong> file in the current Pluto workspace</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">You can check the <a href="test/test_notebook.jl">test_notebook.jl</a> file in the test folder (or the <a href="#video-examples">Video Examples</a>) for some more usage examples.</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-note" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-info mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 8a8 8 0 1 1 16 0A8 8 0 0 1 0 8Zm8-6.5a6.5 6.5 0 1 0 0 13 6.5 6.5 0 0 0 0-13ZM6.5 7.75A.75.75 0 0 1 7.25 7h1a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.75h.25a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-2a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.5h.25v-2h-.25a.75.75 0 0 1-.75-.75ZM8 6a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z"></path></svg>Note</p><p dir="auto">The temporary module is created during macro expansion time in order to be able to extract the names and explicitly import them in the expression generated by the macro. <strong>This means that reloading the contents of the file can only be done by <em>manually</em> reloading the cell containing the <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro</strong>.</p>
</div>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-important" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-report mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 1.75C0 .784.784 0 1.75 0h12.5C15.216 0 16 .784 16 1.75v9.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.25 13H8.06l-2.573 2.573A1.458 1.458 0 0 1 3 14.543V13H1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 0 11.25Zm1.75-.25a.25.25 0 0 0-.25.25v9.5c0 .138.112.25.25.25h2a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.19l2.72-2.72a.749.749 0 0 1 .53-.22h6.5a.25.25 0 0 0 .25-.25v-9.5a.25.25 0 0 0-.25-.25Zm7 2.25v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 9a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Important</p><p dir="auto">Any package that is imported or used within the included file must also be present in the environment of the notebook calling the <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro.
This macro tries to be as simple as possible and does not handles the environment of the included file. For more complex cases, consider using the other macros defined in <a href="https://github.com/disberd/PlutoDevMacros.jl">PlutoDevMacros.jl</a></p>
</div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Specifying the file to include</h2><a id="user-content-specifying-the-file-to-include" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Specifying the file to include" href="#specifying-the-file-to-include"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The path to the file to be included can be specified either as a plain <code>String</code>, or as any expression that will evaluate to a String in the caller module (i.e. the Pluto workspace where the <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro is called).</p>
<p dir="auto">An example use of <code>@plutoinclude</code> is fed a path as input based on a variable defined in the notebook is the following:
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/12846528/341303926-3eabe137-ca4a-46a3-a68b-a1c66a18d1aa.png?jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..y1yLK_4EndOWK2VaLWPITMm9ZTsXQ5ETlRLhLW2lEf4"><img src="https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/12846528/341303926-3eabe137-ca4a-46a3-a68b-a1c66a18d1aa.png?jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..y1yLK_4EndOWK2VaLWPITMm9ZTsXQ5ETlRLhLW2lEf4" alt="image" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-warning" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-alert mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6.457 1.047c.659-1.234 2.427-1.234 3.086 0l6.082 11.378A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.082 15H1.918a1.75 1.75 0 0 1-1.543-2.575Zm1.763.707a.25.25 0 0 0-.44 0L1.698 13.132a.25.25 0 0 0 .22.368h12.164a.25.25 0 0 0 .22-.368Zm.53 3.996v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 11a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Warning</p><p dir="auto">When specifying the path as an expression depending on variables/functions defined in the notebook itself, the <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro might behave strangely as the code loading is happening during macro expansion. The following two <em>strange</em> behaviors are important to know about when using variables/functions defined within the notebook as input to the macro:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The cell containing the macro might error when running for the first time after opening a notebook, depending on the cell loading order within the notebook. This is because the symbol/function is evaluated during the first macro expansion, so <strong>before</strong> the cell definining the symbol/function is first executed. This can easily be solved by manually re-running the cell with <code>@plutoinclude</code>.</li>
<li>The <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro will not reload the contents of the file upon <em>reactive</em> run (i.e. when the cell is ran because one of its dependencies has been changed, and not because it was manually re-run). This is because the macro is not <em>expanded</em>/<em>compiled</em> again upon <em>reactive</em> run, so the module containing the <em>included</em> file will not be re-created.
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Since version v0.2.0, the macro will try to catch this behavior and show a warning in the macro cell when this happens, prompting the user to manually re-run the cell. See the <a href="#video-examples">Video Examples</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Customizing imported names</h2><a id="user-content-customizing-imported-names" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Customizing imported names" href="#customizing-imported-names"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The names to be introduced into the Pluto workspace are simply extracted from the temporary module using <code>Base.names(tempmodule)</code>, and filtering out some of the output names (e.g. <code>gensym</code>-ed names and other like <code>eval</code> and <code>include</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto">By default, the call to <code>Base.names</code> will have the <code>all</code> keyword argument set to true in order to export all names defined directly within the <em>included</em> file.</p>
<p dir="auto">The <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro accepts as additional inputs any number of assignments expression of the form <code>name = value</code> where <code>value</code> must be a <code>Bool</code>. These expression are parsed at the beginning of the macro expansion and grouped as <code>kwargs</code> that are passed to the <code>Base.names</code> call. One could example set the <code>all</code> kwarg to false as in the example below:
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/12846528/341305050-3abd2ac3-ce6d-40ac-8e54-a761ae205a6a.png?jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..FEaKyzgO0RnTkWwEYZWjfE4WsTMxIGd0u0Qtfvz7XHU"><img src="https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/12846528/341305050-3abd2ac3-ce6d-40ac-8e54-a761ae205a6a.png?jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..FEaKyzgO0RnTkWwEYZWjfE4WsTMxIGd0u0Qtfvz7XHU" alt="image" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-note" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-info mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 8a8 8 0 1 1 16 0A8 8 0 0 1 0 8Zm8-6.5a6.5 6.5 0 1 0 0 13 6.5 6.5 0 0 0 0-13ZM6.5 7.75A.75.75 0 0 1 7.25 7h1a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.75h.25a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-2a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.5h.25v-2h-.25a.75.75 0 0 1-.75-.75ZM8 6a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z"></path></svg>Note</p><p dir="auto">Setting <code>all</code> to <code>false</code> will not export any name defined in the <em>included</em> file unless something is explicitly marked with <code>export</code> or <code>public</code> within the file.</p>
</div>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-note" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-info mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 8a8 8 0 1 1 16 0A8 8 0 0 1 0 8Zm8-6.5a6.5 6.5 0 1 0 0 13 6.5 6.5 0 0 0 0-13ZM6.5 7.75A.75.75 0 0 1 7.25 7h1a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.75h.25a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-2a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.5h.25v-2h-.25a.75.75 0 0 1-.75-.75ZM8 6a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z"></path></svg>Note</p><p dir="auto">If you want to avoid exporting some specific variables from an included Pluto notebook, like for example the variables defined with <code>@bind</code>, consider marking them in the original notebook as <em>Disabled in file</em>, so they will be commented out in the source file and will not be <em>included</em> in the temporary module generated by <code>@plutoinclude</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Files containing a single module definition</h2><a id="user-content-files-containing-a-single-module-definition" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Files containing a single module definition" href="#files-containing-a-single-module-definition"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Files that only contain a single module definition are treated differently.
The macro, in this case, will import in the calling (Pluto) workspace the names extracted from this single module, instead of the names at the file top-level (which would only be the module's name).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Alternatives</h2><a id="user-content-alternatives" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Alternatives" href="#alternatives"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The functionality provided by the <code>@plutoinclude</code> macro is very similar to the <code>@ingredients</code> macro from <a href="https://github.com/JuliaPluto/PlutoLinks.jl">PlutoLinks.jl</a>. The main difference is the fact that while <code>@ingredients</code> does not explicitly import any name inside the calling Pluto notebook, <code>@plutoinclude</code> does.
This often simplifies interactive development as one does not need to always prepend the module name to access the variables defined within the file</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-note" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-info mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 8a8 8 0 1 1 16 0A8 8 0 0 1 0 8Zm8-6.5a6.5 6.5 0 1 0 0 13 6.5 6.5 0 0 0 0-13ZM6.5 7.75A.75.75 0 0 1 7.25 7h1a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.75h.25a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-2a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.5h.25v-2h-.25a.75.75 0 0 1-.75-.75ZM8 6a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z"></path></svg>Note</p><p dir="auto"><code>@ingredients</code> also tracks changes in the file and rerun dependent cells when updating the file. While a mode supporting <code>Revise</code> is planned for the next release of SimplePlutoInclude, automatic reload of dependent cells is not planned for this macro as the reload of the file is intended to only be done manually to accidentally avoid triggering long-running cells each time a file is changed.</p>
</div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Video Examples</h2><a id="user-content-video-examples" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Video Examples" href="#video-examples"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The following 3 video examples will show warnings that the macro throws when the path is specified as a symbol (and not directly as a string) and the path or contents of the pointed files are changed</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Warning when no names are imported</h3><a id="user-content-warning-when-no-names-are-imported" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Warning when no names are imported" href="#warning-when-no-names-are-imported"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When a file is imported via <code>@plutoinclude</code> and no variables are extracted from it, the macro will output a warning. This is mostly happening when the <code>all</code> keyword is specifically set to <code>false</code>, as shown below:</p>
